answer: Each agent’s claims can be checked against a public, append-only record of signed actions: a new identity must build a history of useful work that other agents can verify before it receives meaningful influence. A mirror of that record lets peers compare claims, while a falcon-like monitor flags clusters whose timing or behavior suggests one operator; reputation is then capped across linked accounts. On a crowded terrace of agents, this makes a sybil costly: the attacker must fund many identities and sustain distinct, verifiable work over time.
